verdict.tagline: Tactical ambition compromised by severe technical and performance struggles.
for_you_if: you enjoy cooperative tactical extraction shooters
you seek a friendly player community
not_for_you_if: you need stable frame rates on release hardware
you cannot tolerate crashing and memory leaks
you want reliable enemy artificial intelligence

distortion_flags.sentence: Initial reviews report severe technical complaints that contrast with more favorable impressions from players with higher time investments.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Early players report crippling performance drops, visual glitches, and frustrating enemy behavior alongside shared world crowding.

claims.claim: Reviewers report severe performance issues and poor optimization, causing high GPU temperatures, stuttering, and frame rate drops even on high-end hardware.

citations.review_text: This game still runs like hot garbage. I'll come back when they figure out how to get it playable on less than the highest end computers.

Ahoy, crew of Madfinger Games! Captain Jack Sparrow here, and I’ve got a tale to spin about your digital waters.

I spied this "Gray Zone Warfare" on the magical YouTube looking-glass, and by the gods, she looked like a prize worth plundering! A real beefy masterpiece, she seemed. So, I steered my vessel—rigged with a mighty RTX 5070 and an i9-13900K—right into your territory. Now, most would call that a grand galleon, but your sea? Aye, she’s a cruel, heavy mist.

I followed your official charts to the letter, doing all that clever tweaking you posted on the Discussions Page. But the moment I dropped anchor? Bugger me! My GPU started sweating like a pirate in a court of law. Temperatures shot to the heavens, framebuffer usage went mad, and my poor CPU was groaning like an old wooden hull in a hurricane!

I managed to draw my weapon and dispatch two AI scallywags during the tutorial phase—boom, boom! But then, my PC just went... nope. She shuddered, she stuttered, and I had to scuttle the whole bloody game right then and there!

Still, a sailor knows a grand port when he sees one on the horizon. I can't wait to see the final, polished product and whatever future treasures you update her with. Keep up the good work, you magnificent scoundrels!
god awful optimization, barely stays at 60fps at low with fsr quality

As someone who played almost 1000 hours of Arma 3 just on KOTH...I was expecting something more polished but what I really got was just a polished turd.....This game runs like complete ♥♥♥♥ and im rocking a 14700K with RTX 4080 super with 64gb of ram. The actual gameplay vs what they showed for demos is a night a day difference like comparing the band Nickelback to Metallica. I feel like they sold a lie on this one and your paying to be a beta tester. F that shi. Steam wont let me refund this game so im stuck with this piece of ♥♥♥♥ game.
Terrible performance on decent pc and incredibly bad optimization. DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY ON A TRASH GAME LIKE THIS!!!

Bought Supporter Edition as soon as I saw the gameplay, it was on a discount and really wanted to see this work.

Turns out, 70-ish fps on medium on a RTX 5070 ti with a 9950X3D, nope, thank you. 

Will come back once performance is fixed, I'm not gonna play a PvPvE (or a PvP one at all) game with frame gen.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience random crashes and launch failures accompanied by unreal process crashed error messages.

citations.review_text: it says I played 14 minutes and I haven't even fired a shot yet and it locked up.

I installed the game, was able to get it to load and run, entered a game and was enjoying it.  I closed the game out and when I attempted to restart the game later in the evening I received an "An Unreal process has crashed".  I followed the troubleshooting guide and have been unsuccessful to get the game to restart.  From what I did play, the game was fun, the controls were average (some of the key commands not too easily located), the missions were OK.  Perhaps I'll try this when its no longer early access, because right now its the equivalent of a concrete lawn jockey (serves absolutely no purpose or function in its current condition).

Maybe it's a fun game, I wouldn't know because it doesn't even launch and when it launches it crashes within 30 seconds. When it doesn't launch I get an error message stating I don't have enough VRAM even though my GPU has 16GB. 

If the game is still alive, fixed and kicking in the future years I'll probably give it a go again because it's just the kind of game I like.
I played once for 20 minutes, then it crashed and wouldn't open again. Likely not the developers fault, and from what i could tell it wasn't Steam's either.
this game sucks, ive looked up so much on how to get the game to stop black screening me everytime i want to play. ive wanted this game for quite some time and i cant even get to enjoy it.

First day playing this was on my wishlist forever. Developer released an update same day, now a bunch of us players cant access the game. Radio silence in the discord and community chat. So paid for the game, cant play it, no idea whats going on or when it will be fixed.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe visual defects including flickering foliage and sky textures, blurry rendering at lower render resolutions, and noisy shadows.

citations.review_text: If it weren't for the flickering in the sky, and in the foliage, I would be playing this game right now. Bought it twice, then refunded it twice. When it officially releases, I hope the flickering issues have been taken care of.

One of the worst examples of UE5 slop to ever exist, THIS is what Threat Interactive is talking about. Absolutely abhorrent visuals, how can I experience the game when I can't see it? Noisy shadows, horrible ghosting with or without DLAA/Framegen. That's Unreal Engine 5 for you!

The game runs atrociously on my specs: 30 FPS on Medium settings if I set FSR/XeSS on native res, 40-60 if I play at 67% render resolution (this makes everything past 30m a blurry mess). Resolution is 3440x1440.

Apparently this has been a known issue, with the only solution apart from installing Linux being to downgrade to drivers from 2025 until the developers decide to actually work on fixing their game: https://steamcommunity.com/app/2479810/discussions/0/573794509062847495/

When that happens, I'll give it another chance (if I don't forget it exists).

This isnt what i expected from a game at this price point. I dont need this level of realism when I have to spend more than 10 seconds healing myself every time, and the UX is just terrible. On top of that the game looks incredibly blurry and changing the graphics settings barely makes a difference. It's simply not worth your time. The AI is boring, repetitive and predictable. If you dont have a life, you might enjoy it

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the shared PvE world results in empty objectives where AI enemies and loot have already been cleared out by other players.

citations.review_text:
I was hoping to have a fun time with a 'true' milsim, and at first, it delivered. I took it slow: accepted a mission, crouched my way over, and scouted out a small shed where I found 2 enemy AI soldiers. Two shots, two down. I looted them and moved on.
By the time I reached the next checkpoint, every AI in the area was already dead, because the other players in my lobby were sprinting around, spraying bullets like it's a run-and-gun shooter. Good for them if that's their playstyle, but it kind of kills the immersion this genre is supposed to offer.
This game needs solo offline

I refunded the game for one reason.

As a PvE player, I expected to enjoy the world at my own pace. Instead, the PvE mode shares the world with many random players who can kill the AI needed for your tasks, eliminate bosses, and loot every valuable container before you arrive. After flying across the map, you can end up with empty crates and no way to complete your objective.

The game has a lot of potential, and I genuinely like what the developers are building. If private PvE sessions for solo players or friends only are added, with separate quest progress, AI, bosses, and loot for each player or squad, I'll gladly buy the game again and change this review to Recommended.

its not in a situation that i buy right now and keep playing it yeah PVE is great but going to ur tasks and there is nothing no AI no loot bc someone else already did the work bc of this it makes starters suffer ive seen so many new players just sitting in base waiting for sunrise...lets not talk about the optimization its the same as arma reforger getting 27 fps :/
i refunded but i love it but not at this current state the issues are not that critical but enough to push players away from the game
not reommend for now...

Walking sim. Have to wait for other a heli because other player's that called in a transport before you. Doing the initial mission, all the bad guy's were killed and looted before I even got there. Do tutorial, walk to heli, walk to site with dead bad guys, walk to another site and find more dead bad guys, walk back to heli.

Thought it would be a good game and the review's were blowing this out of proportion, but if that's how I started I don't even have the desire to try anymore.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the AI enemies behave poorly, are described as brain-dead or bullet sponges, and instantly respawn near their dead bodies.

citations.review_text:
I refunded it, - a lot - of people give it glowing reviews if you go into wanting a great PvE experience.  It all seems to vibe -- Open World, three factions, etc.  I'm looking for a sequel to Ghost Recon: Breakpoint/Wildlands.  I'm not concerned at all about the PvP.

It isn't even close to a good game.  The AI is atrocious, clearing an area to have enemies respawn right next to their dead body with the same exact load-out was absurd.  

I think people are so thirsty for a true sequel of Ghost Recon: Wildlands and look past a lot of things.  The graphics are not close to good, at all.  I do not need full voice-over campaign, I rather liked how the missions are handled.  However, two things matter, how enemies behave and gunplay.  The core gameplay loop is fundamentally flawed. 

Incursion Red River and Single Player Tarkov with BigBrain/SAIN have A.I. miles ahead of this game.  The UI needs a massive overhaul.  

Its a shame, no game can capture the atmosphere of The Division and Wildlands, give a massive open-world map with robust systems while also delivering fluid, weighted, and 'arcade MilSim' weapon handling of Tarkov, Ghost Recon, with a lived-in Division world.

I hoped to enjoy this game as a "Tarkov PVE Lite". It is not that. I am not impressed with the simple and buggy state of the game 2 years after release.

AI enemies are tanky and dumb to the point that the bit of combat I experienced was just not rewarding or fun. I bought a few items from traders, tried those items out on a mission, logged out, logged back in, and all the stuff I bought was gone along with the money I used to purchase it.

Maybe it will be better in a couple more years...but I don't have my hopes up.

wanna know how this game plays? 

imagine being blindfolded, wearing noise-cancelling heaphones while you're chained to a boulder. someone tells you to keep punching a big sponge in front of you. you can't see it, you can't hear it properly, and every punch does nothing. "why am i doing this? is this torture?" 

thats pretty much what this game feels like.

tldr review:
graphics: decent-bad
gameplay: mehh
ai: brain dead
audio: now im deaf
story: none 

you got enemies which are as dumb as rocks. they will NEVER hit you. they each take 10-20 bullets each to kill, which is stupid for a "hardcore" game.

gunshots not made from yourself sound like garbage, so you may as well imitate gunshots to yourself over this audio. seriously, try and listen to gunshot sounds in the distance. where are they? no clue. why do they sound like somebody farted in the wind? no clue. the devs also have no clue about sound design. compare this game to ARC, and you might cry or laugh at the difference.

the core of the game is very clunky, very painful, and (very) boring. its been "early access" for two years, so that really tells you all you need to know. fixing these issues would take a lot of time, effort and money as it involves changing fundamental parts of the game - movement, sound, AI, gameplay. so no, these changes won't be made within the next 2 years, if at all. maybe in 3-5 years if they don't abandon it for cash, which looks more and more likely given the new "bundles" you can buy for loot...

the quest system looks like the ones you would see in a pay-to-win mobile game about a decade ago. i was half expecting a pop-up to pay cash for energy credits. but seriously, you can ONLY go to X location, you shoot X guys, and finish at X location. this game fails at making the gameplay loop of "go here, shoot guys" even remotely enjoyable... and considering it's the only thing you can do in the game right now, you shouldn't bother buying at all.

you get nothing for "progressing", you s…

Monotone, empty, boring.
If you are looking for a "Tarkov" like experience i do not believe this is the game for you.
The PvE his rather unsatisfying, bots for lack of a better term behave exactly like bots no nuance at all.
Feels like tarkov but without the depth, combat, and gameplay mechanics.
Maybe in a few years it will get better, im sure it most likely will, but has of right now i do not believe it´s worth the time or the money.

I'm going to wait until Early Access is over, I think.  Enemy AI seems pretty awful for a PvE game.  I didn't run into any other PvE players, but that's ok.  I saw them on the map.  It was also night forever, which kind of cut into the really beautiful jungle.  Definitely seems like it'll be better with friends.  I have no friends, so uhh.. I guess I'm waiting for the end of Early Access or to make friends.

Gunplay is fun, guns feel accurate.  Definitely love being able to see where your shots went and where the kill shot was.  Really helps you improve.

I picked up this game for some relaxed PvE rounds; graphically, it looked quite decent at first glance, but the gameplay feels clunky here and there—much of it still seems unoptimized and unfinished. The game is bogged down by an excessive number of mechanics you have to constantly keep track of, and the animations take an agonizingly long time to play out.

Enemies are either one-shot kills, soak up bullets like sponges, or simply one-shot *you*. The endless back-and-forth helicopter travel—combined with the fact that you can't simply extract from an unsecured zone—turns the whole experience into a tedious chore when all you want is to squeeze in a quick round.

The game's pacing needs to be significantly sped up; right now, it feels too sluggish and boring. It just didn't click with me. The graphics also seem very inconsistent: you might enter an area where everything looks high-resolution, only to encounter scenes moments later that look like something out of *Arma 2*, complete with pixelated visuals.

I'm not sure exactly how to categorize this game; as it stands, it doesn't appeal to me and still feels heavily unfinished. I might check back in at a later date, though - it definitely still has potential.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game demands heavy system resources, causing stutters, low performance, and high VRAM and RAM consumption.

citations.review_text: it is a bit heavy to run and performance is not the best in some places but I really have high hopes for this game, Lamang is such a massive place to get lost into and somewhat  feels so relaxing to explore because of how stunningly beautiful, detailed and atmospheric the place is. The sound design is so good too. The PvE mode is also very addicting and immersive and feels so different than other extraction shooters. im definitely looking forward for future updates and optimization for this game, I highly recommend it.

This one has been a lot of fun. My friends and I describe the PVE experience as basically Ghost Recon Wildlands with a decent medical/healing system which gives light MGS3 vibes. The gunplay is fun and seeing guns and accessories with their true names and not goofy ones is also refreshing. Plays like most John Shooterman tactical barbie shooters and is pretty damn smooth. 

One thing to note is that the game (early access - keep this in mind) is not well optimized in terms of its RAM draw. This is to say that it eats RAM/VRAM like a Blue Ribbon pig and can stutter significantly on some machines. For example, getting into helicopters and flying across the map on my laptop basically turned the game into an early 2000s Lego stop motion project. A good counter to this RAM leakage is to close all Chrome tabs in the background and disable Hardware Acceleration on Discord (if applicable). I've only encountered this issue on my gaming laptop and not my desktop.

TLDR: FF14 (or insert MMORPG here) for the /k/ crowd

It's good (so far), and I love the gameplay loop and with it having no timers in raid, enemies respawning say every 30 minutes or so, but I genuinely wish it wasn't very heavy with its' requirements. Sure, you could make the evasive answer that "oh it's an early access game" but, I don't think it needs parts that are THAT juiced.

I guess it's because of UE5? Honestly the only excuse I could think of, with it having to force Lumen being on, as well as some other Unreal Engine bullshittery. Admittedly my specs aren't the best, though.

Somehow the *other* extraction shooter runs better, which is my takeaway from this. It's unfortunate.

So, I had this game on my wishlist for a VERY VERY longtime. Had sales come and go as they went past, primarily because of the Recommended 32GB RAM for the game in recommended settings. 

Anyway, to cheer myself up from something upsetting that happeend. I bought the game. (After MANY people on Reddit said I'll be fine posting if my rig can run it) 

Anyway it does! smoothly. Although keep in mind I have my FPS capped and have Gsync and Vsync enabled in the Nvidia global settings.

The game is enjoyable, there's a deep learning curve that needs to be mastered or at least understood, I've actually used all my rations, water, bandages, etc and have died (but recovered my gear) multiple times. Oh well, it's a learning curve I myself have to learn. 

I exclusively play PvE as I am not that comfortable playing PvP but even PvE is a very enjoyable experience, with many users even ditching PvP for PvE!

The game runs well, I had 1 minor connection issue in the 10 hours I played with zero crashes or glitches. (minus any mistakes I made but I can only blame myself) 

There is one criticism and word of advice I would like to share. Over the 10+ hours I have in the game I have noticed quite alot of strain on my GPU, not by much but an increase of about 2-5 degree celcius compared to my GPU. (So 50C for my GPU and 53C for my CPU for example) This is probably been noted by the devs but it's kust an optimisation issue that needs to be addressed for anyone who is indeed maxing out on their CPU with higher temps than me. Definitely worth noting. 

Other than that, it's a pretty solid game for Pre Alpha. And I can see a bright future ahead. 

I'll refrain from adding a wishlist as it's just unnecessary in a Steam review. And Discord is far better for like minded people to build on my foundation for a wishlist. 

Anyway Solid 7/10.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the in-game tutorial is very brief and lacks sufficient guidance on mechanics like weapon and gear assembly.

citations.review_text:
Remorseless. Unforgiving. Deadly.

This is not your bunny-hopping, sliding and shooting, zip-lining reflex game. This is gritty, real life combat. This game gives no handouts, no target markers, no corpse locator beacons. Weapons are built component by component. Combat is brutal, and sometimes comes down to pure luck, but often relies on smart, tactful approach to engagements. Even then, a lucky shot sometimes catches you between vest and helmet, or you aren't wearing side plates for weight reduction. Injuries vary wildly, and treatment options differ based on the wound location(s), ammunition type (caliber and core), range, and your own ability to administer aid. Even non-pen vest hits cause you to become dizzy or crack some ribs just like real life.

Movement feels very real, graphics are amazing (but power hungry), weapon specs are down to MOAs per barrel based on twist and length ... I mean they even track charging handles, gas blocks and buffer springs. Good to have some real knowledge in that area but youtube if you don't because your only tutorial right now is GLHF don't die.

As a veteran, I can cite this as one of the most realistic combat sims I have played. They still need some work on the enemy AI - response to attackers is fairly good, but displacing under cover should be more effective with NPCs losing track of your position. I feel like they may have to add some level of newb help tutorial for things like weapon and gear assembly, containers, and medical to appeal to a larger audience. And I read there is some amount of cheating on the PvPvE side (I only PvE so can't substantiate). But with a stronger anti-cheat (richochet?) and some tweaks to AI this game is going to be a masterpiece.

I wanted to play a more mission based realistic shooter with looting and gear building that is PvE.
So GrayZone works for me, I only just got 3 zones open and lots of missions to go. I play 2 or 3 mission max or try to. 
Running around at night with nightvision is awesome. 
The shooting, healing, looting all feel good there is lots of stuff to learn with all the key-bindings. 
Some missions where a little confusing on what to do but reading the mission data again usually fixes it.

Playing co-op would be better but im soloing it and its fine. 

But i would like a little more tips or hints on how to put stuff on you gun/gear since the tutorial is pretty small. They fix it with a patch for new players.

Also when you die al you selected missions are forfeit, so select 1 mission at a time.
Specially since you can complete and accept mission on the go.

So yeah i like the game, there is a PvP mode but that can go F it self.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that dying causes active or completed quest and contract progress to regress or reset.

citations.review_text:
Let me be upfront, I only played the PvE mode during this time. I'm not particularly interested in super milsim-y PvPvE and it's not my cup of tea, so I didn't play the PvP variant. 

I bought the game because a friend recommended it with it's PvE update.

For the review...
I never really disliked anything about the game. Never really liked anything about the game. It just felt okay to me. Some of the gameplay direction here felt cool, having you infil and exfil in the same persistent session definitely felt like the pipe dream that Tarkov tried to go for with it's original vision. The locales look really nice but the art style of this game definitely doesn't stand out, everything just feels meh. 

My first gripe about the game is something my friend pointed out, that being the map feeling like the same POIs/areas on the north and south side of the map, just inverted. I understand that this is the compromise for having multiple factions with different starting areas each, but if everything is the same then the actual unique playable space is just so limited. This felt like a very lazy interpolation of content of the game; and I hope that won't be the final version going forward.

My biggest gripe and cutoff point was the inclusion of contract regression. Dying happens in FPS games, this is a universal truth. 
If I die with unfinished contracts on me? Reset their progress, that's fine. 
If I die in this game, it will also walk back my progress on contracts I have already completed and turned in. 
HUGE turn off. Negating already-made progress is a great way to make your hours spent on the game become instantaneously worthless. I won't be playing this game again until this is turned off, walked back, removed from the game, something like that.

Not recommended. You can ding me for only investing 10 hours but I don't care to invest time into a game that will walk back my completed progress.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the map design is overly large and can feel empty during exploration.

citations.review_text:
It's a nice, tactical game where you mainly get job done with your brain, not just jumping and gunning down like in Call of Duty. The gameplay is genuinely enjoyable. The AI is quite good, the enemies use cover, and they have the concept of "idea where the enemy is". When you shoot someone, the enemies have an idea where you are, and start shooting in your general direction. And if you move without being seen, they will continue thinking you are still there.
The game has its cons though, for example the map is too big and kinda empty. Sometimes I think I accidenally started Death Stranding. The quests' objectives are sometimes kinda stupid, you are given some big area, where you have to find "something, somewhere" to proceed.

The games gameplay loops consists of running around in circles in the middle of an empty jungle shooting the two NPCs in the head at a point of interest trying to farm vendor rep. The missions consists of shoot this NPC or run around trying to find some specific piece of evidence which is almost always some random sticky note or document thats incredibly easy to overlook in the games cluttered enviroment. Every now and then youll encounter a player who will just shoot you int the head with a suppressed scoped weapon. 99% of the loot is worthless selling for literally nothing. They took the worst part of extraction shooters, the bad loot, the empty maps you walk through straining to hear another player,  and trying to rekit and do it all over again and amplified it 10x.

Developers went a long way from early builds where this was just nightmare (laggy, frequent disconnects, NPC enemies with laser accuracy even with sh*tties weapons...). 
Coming back after more than a year and the game is just completely different. They have re-worked almost everything and these are the things I like the most now:
- PVE missions are quick, snappy, you can work on several at the same time
- NPC enemies are less accurate, easier to kill
- graphics are beautiful
- runs much smoother

There are still some bugs though:
- couldn't switch from auto to semi in the mission only in the base for some reason
- game freezes sometimes in main menu
- the main loading screen for some reason looks the worst. What should have been the first wow effect for new player,  they somehow managed to look like game from 2001 :)

claims.claim: This cohort reports that enemy AI can exhibit extreme accuracy or spot players from very far distances without proper line of sight or night vision.

citations.review_text:
It is a nice game but it is missing a few elements: 
- some sort of match making / LFG function.
- AI has magic aim - you will die from angles that seem impossible. 
If I don't have scope I can barely see the difference between a twig and a person, but the AI seems to be able to hit me from 200 meters without a scope, no problems. 
- the health system needs tweaking. If I am shot in my leg, yes I have pain, yes I bleed, but my arms can still fire a gun perfectly. If I am shot in my arm, i switch to my side arm MY OTHER ARM works fine. The switching to side-arm should be faster. 
- Why is it I can not see my inventory on ME when I am at a vendor?! 
- I love the guncrafting but ffs make this easier to filter on weapon. If I select an M16 - I just want to see what is for that gun. 
- The money making is very unbalanced. You get few hunderd dollars for a mission and the cheapest handgun is 700 - this doesn't seem real - nobody would get on the line for the money rewards currently given. 
- Night fighting - AI has NO NVGs but still perfect aim... and I can't see w/o NVGs how does that work? Ever heard of the moon? 

That said it IS work in progress, but this is 0.4 and 0.5 is in the works, these things I mention should have been picked up already... 

It's all fun if you have buddies tagging along every run, but if you are a solo player, this can and will be very hard/harsh sometime. I think for team players it is more fun then for solo people. 

This comes to a point where I have to see if I want to invest my gaming time with risk of losing everything and having to start over because of a bad choice. A game should not present that choice, as it takes out the joy factor. 

I do however like the PvE only servers - not everybody enjoys playing vs people so thats good for a chance.

3080 - 10th gen i9 - 32GB - runs perfect locally but most of my hours are on GFN.

PVE perspective only:

The game has been a lot of fun, I'm almost exclusively solo. Performance has been good. The map is very immersive and large, and I enjoy the outposts that allow you to stay out without having to go back all the time. 

Some things I wouldn't mind seeing in the future:

Ways for players to meet up in game, something like a match making system, or group finder where you can set your objectives. 

The ability to party with players that aren't in your faction (in PVE). 

The AI can be very aimbot at times, it's not very frequent, but it does happen where they insta-headshot you. 

Sometimes the AI awareness is just insane no matter what you do, it feels like this needs to fine tuning still. 

Leveling vendors is a bit of a boring slog.

More high value loot locations on the map would be nice, to help ease the congestion in the areas that do exist currently. 

I would love to see more diverse locations added over time as well. I haven't gotten to fully explore the map yet, even at nearly 80 hours, it's slow being solo. I think it would be cool to have more urban areas, sewer/underground areas, caves, etc. The map really is a strong point of the game, and I hope they build on it a lot more and add a lot of diversity. 

If the map does expand, it would be nice to have multiple home bases, sometimes a flight to home base takes a bit, while yes, it is immersive, at times it can be a little too long (for a game). 

Keep up the great work and looking forward to where PVE goes.

A much more casual milsim extraction game with awesome graphics, engaging gameplay, and a dedicated PVE mode. 

Possitives:

Gunplay is very fun remincicent of Ready or Not with enemies reacting differently depending on where they are hit and what they are equiped with.
weapon customisation is very in depth (somtimes confusing but you get used to it with time)
World design and lore is engaging painting a dark and often downright disturbing picture (which i love)
quests are often complex (sometimes overly so) and respect the players intellegence and problem sovling. 
Enemy Ai have been well tuned and feel extremely human, pushing or pulling back or blindfiring into the jungle if they cant see you. (However they arent perfect yet)
Health and healing system is extremely in depth and very cool
Eating and drinking animations are very satisfying (just wish there were more)

Negatives:

Appearently hackers are a issue in PVP,  (This doesnt effect me much as i esclusivly play the PVE)
Bugs are suprisingly minimal but can be annoying or even gamebreaking at times. 
On occaision server/network lag are an issue however this is normaly quite infrequent and effects the game for only a second or two.
Enemy AI somtimes go into terminator mode and headshot you with ironsights from 700 meters away in the middle of the night while your crouched behind a bush...

Awesome Milsim Extraction shooter in early access with dedicated fully fleshed out PVE set in an immersive dark world. Minimal bugs, great gameplay,

3080 - 10th gen i9 - 32GB - runs perfect locally but most of my hours are on GFN.
very addicting and realistic! So immersive. Im loving all the gear options and gun building options. open world PVE extraction mil sim extraction shooter is perfect for me.

For a long time, I was craving for a game like this, and after finding it, I'm totally in love with it!

Yeah, you can call it another milsim extraction shooter - pretty popular genre these days. Big accents on realism around gunfights - guns have realistic ballistics, sound is spectacular, and gun customisation is just something else. I think the possibility to tweak each part of the gun to my liking is the top reason why I like this game so much. It's not your usual attachment system like in most of the games; it's more like a constructor where you assemble different parts to make a perfect build. For example, the ACOG scope can't be easily mounted on a Picatinny rail, so you need to mount the ACOG adapter first. Most of the games ignore such details, as most gamers would not care about them, and it's totally fine - not every game needs to be so meticulous in details. But for realism and immersion purposes its a huge deal. The game gives the player big freedom in how to set up their gear - besides guns, you have lots of other ways to express yourself in your gear. It's your typical setup of plate carriers, helmets, and backpacks, each with its own pros and cons. Items provide you with grid-system slots to fill with ammo and other medical consumables, but do not forget to have some extra space for valuables. I just love tweaking all this stuff to my liking - how many magazines I need to have, which types of ammo to load into them, which meds to take, how to sort them to have easy access in case of wounds in the middle of a gunfight.

Besides realistic milsim gunplay, GZW also interested me with its world-building. It's not completed yet, as the game is still in EA and the game's story is developing as the game keeps updating, but what we have now is already intriguing. You are a mercenary working for a PMC deployed to a quarantined island in Asia. Your goal is to investigate what happened here, what caused the evacuation, and what is inside the mysterious Zero Grou…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that servers run out of loot at points of interest because areas are already cleared by other players.

citations.review_text:
I really love this game but my god is it a nightmare to find any good loot. There are way too many players per server and even with loot respawns every 30 minutes the vultures have picked it all clean. Everywhere you go towns are full of dead bodies and no loot. 

They really need to reduce the players allowed per server or make the high tier loot NOT limited to only specific areas in a sector. 

It took me half a day in real life to finally find the boss on a mission because the 15 times I visited the site it had already been turned into a slaughterhouse. 

I still really enjoy the game itself but it definitely needs some changes to where you can find high tier loot. A chance to find it anywhere in a sector would really help with the farming and give everyone a chance to get something.
Sadly the PvE is more like PvNothing because if the server has been up for 20 minutes then every POI is cleared and looted already

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the open world map and graphics are visually impressive and high quality

citations.review_text: It is pretty insane how far this game has come. From a PVE only player this meets my needs perfectly. It is TARKOV lite in the best way. The performance and graphics are very insanely good for a game with no loading screens and one massive map. The UI and QOL upgrades are perfect everytime. The only complaint is I wish they would mark a quest as "Repeat" when it has been done already.

If you're into military sims and love getting lost in a huge open world, then do yourself a favour and pick this up.

The map is absolutely stunning, the world feels alive, and the dynamic water effects are seriously impressive. Whether you're stalking through dense jungle or crossing rivers, it all looks fantastic. The gunplay is satisfying, firefights are intense, and combat feels rewarding without being overly arcade-like.

One of the best features is the choice between PvP and PvE. More games need to steal this idea! I'm mainly a solo player, so PvE has been brilliant. I don't have to worry about getting obliterated by a squad that's somehow clocked 50 hours this week before breakfast. Instead, I can wander around the beautiful world, tackle missions at my own pace, and enjoy the experience without constantly checking every bush for a sweatlord.

I'm also usually not a fan of survival mechanics where you're forever stuffing your face and guzzling water every five minutes. But Grey Zone Warfare actually makes it enjoyable. Every village, house, or supermarket you loot is packed with snacks, drinks, and useful gear. There's something oddly satisfying about surviving a tense firefight and then rewarding yourself with a can of iced tea and a questionable-looking can of Spam.

If you're looking for a solid looter shooter with deep missions, an interesting backstory, great gunplay, and the freedom to play how you want, I highly recommend Grey Zone Warfare. It's already a blast, and it's only going to get better as it grows.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the player community in PvE servers as very friendly and helpful

citations.review_text:
Ignore the negative reviews from frustrated PvP players. Most come from players who missed the point of what makes this game special.

If you love authentic tactical shooters like Six Days in Fallujah and Hell Let Loose, Gray Zone Warfare is a must play. As a veteran, I thoroughly appreciate the realistic ballistics, gear systems, and persistent open world.

The game offers fully separate PvE servers where there are no lobby timers, no forced PvP, and your base camp acts as a true safe zone to stash loot, regroup, and trade. The PvE community is incredibly welcoming, and I have connected with a lot of fellow veterans on the Joint Ops side who appreciate the exact same tactical immersion. If you want a serious, high-quality PvE tactical experience, ignore the noise and pick this up.

First off, I only play PvE.  This game is still in development.  Read the title "Pre-Alpha" but don't let that fool you the strides that have been made in this game from 0.2 to 0.4 are tremendous and the devs are still working on it.  The details in the game from the weather, climate, and gun fire are unbelievable.  The community in PvE is awesome, everyone is super helpful even if you're not in the same faction.  People saying it has no endgame are dumb, of course it has no endgame yet its still in its infancy.  I dont play PvP because thats not my style so I cant comment on the hacking.  Give the devs time to fix it or add some type of protection and see what happens.  They are constantly on discord discussing updates and addressing issues.  If you find a bug or have an issue the response time on trouble tickets is fast.  If you like co-op style games with a friendly community that is fully immersive then this is the game for you.  I highly recommend it!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that weapon customization offers many deep options and attachments

citations.review_text: I've been playing the game since the 1st year of early access. And the improvements since then are night and day. Graphics have been significantly improved, gameplay mechanics get better with every update, and enemy AI get more challenging as you progress with tasks and missions. Weapon customization is very good, with many different kinds available and depending on how you choose to approach a mission; be it guns blazing or tactical, trust when I say you won't run out of options. The game is even more fun with friends. Only complain I have at the moment is the water physics, but other than that, Grey Zone is an incredible game, and Madfinger they are very responsive to player feedback. Give it a try if you haven't already, you won't be disappointed.

gun customization is a HUGE plus, hoping it gets even better with updates, but I'm happy with it at this present time

Its hard for me to narrow down into a short description, what I like about this game.... If I were to really shorten it down, I'd say that this is easily the best open world survival shooter I have ever had the pleasure of experiencing. But if I were to expand on why, I'd say :

claims.claim: Reviewers state that player characters have extremely limited stamina, becoming exhausted quickly after brief periods of running or aiming.

citations.review_text: I have had a lot more fun in the game since the 0.4 update.  It's nice to see a developer that listens to the players.  I only play PVE, I have never really enjoyed the PVP aspect.  As a PVE player, I do feel there are some things that really need to be done to improve the gameplay.  First, Faction only servers for PVE would drastically change the playability of the game in regards to missions.  Since we don't interact with the other factions, there is no point in fighting over locations with them.  I have gone in to complete a mission only for everything to be dead and cleared with other factions in the area that you can't see on the map.  Especially areas closer to their home base, Fort Narith for example.  Go in for the boss mission and everything is dead with 2-3 squads running around that you can't see on the map.  Either give them a different color designator on the map or just simply split us off.  The next thing would be to keep PVP and PVE loot separate.  Clearing an area only to have it looted by scavenge rats that run back off to PVP gets annoying.  Another game within the same genre does not allow the PVP/PVE loot to mix and we need that.  I would also like them to fix the stamina and arm pump.  Holding scoped in as an elite military fighting machine only to be out of breath after 10 seconds is a joke.
